subject: Hosted evaluation: quick plan & ratecap check
body:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Ellie Cooper <ellie@finlytics.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-15 14:05 PT
Subject: Hosted evaluation: quick plan & ratecap check

Hi Ellie / team,

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier — really appreciated the clear product problems you walked through. This note is a short recap + proposed next steps so we can get your Hosted evaluation up and running this week.

Recap of what we heard during the call:
- Primary goal: test model-driven document summarization and inline-answer features for the customer support vertical (pre-production).
- Success criteria for evaluation: 200ms p95 for the synchronously-called summarization endpoint, quality match to your existing baseline, and workable cost estimates for production.
- Production preference: you mentioned Private/VPC for legal reasons ultimately, but you wanted to run a Hosted evaluation first to validate latency/quality and integrations.

Requests we need from you to configure a Hosted trial environment:
1) Traffic profile (sample): average requests/sec, peak RPS, average tokens per request, expected concurrency.
2) Sample payloads or a small prompt set we can use for evals (anonymized is fine).
3) Any strict privacy/data residency requirements for the trial (e.g., EU-only endpoints).

What Redwood will provision for the Hosted evaluation:
- Two-week trial API key with dedicated sandbox endpoint(s).
- Endpoint mapping: /summarize (sync), /chat (optional), and a short-lived embedding endpoint for search tuning.
- Rate caps and quota: we can set a conservative default and bump to your requested levels after we verify traffic patterns.
- Observability: token usage, per-request latency, and example-level quality metrics in the Console.

Attachments: I attached a quick Excel template (FinLytics_Rate_Profile.xlsx) — please fill the highlighted rows so we can size the trial rate caps properly.

Proposed next steps / timeline:
- You fill the rate profile and drop it back by EOD tomorrow.
- If numbers align, we schedule a 45-min tech kickoff (integration and test plan) — propose Thu Mar 18, 10:00 AM PT.
- I'll provision trial keys and forwarding logs once we confirm the kickoff slot.

Can you confirm the proposed kickoff time and share the rate profile? If hosted looks good, we can document the Private/VPC requirements for a later stage and loop in Security/Compliance.

Thanks,
--
Priyom Das
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
priom.das@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

----

From: Ellie Cooper <ellie@finlytics.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Owen Price <owen.price@finlytics.com>
Date: 2028-03-15 17:20 ET
Subject: Re: Hosted evaluation: quick plan & ratecap check

Hi Priyom — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the traffic profile so you can size the Hosted trial:
- Avg requests: ~3 requests/sec during working hours (09:00–18:00 ET)
- Burst: up to ~30 requests/sec for short bursts (~2–3 min)
- Avg tokens per request: 250 tokens (some longer customer threads up to 1,200 tokens occasionally)
- Peak token throughput estimate: ~45,000 tokens/minute at peak burst
- Target latency: p95 <= 200ms (we know this is tight; the goal is to see feasibility with a minimal model variant)

Notes:
- For evaluation we are fine using Hosted. Production likely needs Private VPC (compliance with our data retention policy) — we flagged that for later.
- We can provide anonymized prompt samples and a small set of reference outputs by EOD tomorrow.

Confirming Thu Mar 18, 10:00 AM PT for a technical kickoff works for our engineers. Please provision a sandbox API key and set the initial rate caps conservatively (something like 50 RPS burst and a 5 RPS steady cap until we validate).

I'll attach the sample payloads to my next email.

Best,
Ellie
Ellie Cooper
Head of Product, FinLytics
ellie@finlytics.com

----

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Ellie Cooper <ellie@finlytics.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-15 22:00Z
Subject: Re: Hosted evaluation: quick plan & ratecap check

Ellie — perfect, thanks for the numbers. We'll start with a conservative Hosted sandbox config and iterate once we see real traffic:
- Sandbox defaults: steady 5 RPS, short-burst allowance up to 60 RPS with token-based throttling.
- We'll map endpoints: /v1/summarize (sync, 250 token avg) and /v1/chat for multi-turn.
- We'll also enable prefix caching for repeated customer templates to reduce cost.

Next steps from Redwood: I'll provision the sandbox API key and share the key + endpoint details and a Quickstart doc before the tech kickoff. We'll also pre-configure the trial rate caps per your ask; we can adjust in the first 24 hours after the kickoff.

Attachments: prod-demo-screenshot.png (screenshot of Console token breakdown — FYI).

See you Thu 10:00 AM PT — I'll send a calendar invite with dial-in details.

Thanks,
--
Priyom

----

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-16 03:12Z
Subject: Internal: FinLytics hosted trial config (action items)

Team — internal action items before Thu kickoff (ticket OPS-1423):
1) Provision sandbox tenant for FinLytics, tag with deal RDW-2028-77-FIN.
2) Create API key with initial quotas: steady 5 RPS, burst up to 60 RPS, token throttle set at 75,000 tokens/min during burst.
3) Pre-map endpoints: /v1/summarize -> model: redwood-2-small (can failover to redwood-2-medium), /v1/chat for multi-turn.
4) Enable Console traces and forward example requests to the eval project. Add logging retention 30 days.
5) Add monitoring alert for p95 latency > 350ms and token usage > 80% of quota.

Sean — can you own the provisioning and the runbook for the trial environment? Aditya — please prepare a short run-through deck (10 slides) for the kickoff showing how to hit the endpoints and where to find token/latency dashboards.

I'll follow up once the key is created and when the calendar invite is accepted.

Thanks,
Priyom
